calls.head: Strength vs. Strength
calls.body: The Sabres are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Kings’ defense.
calls.call: The Kings keep the Sabres’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot).

surprises.head: Buffalo couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Buffalo’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.3% against Los Angeles) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Los Angeles shortened their bench
surprises.body: Los Angeles usually uses their bottom six less than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a short bench: the bottom six played 34% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Luukkonen steals one in Los Angeles
paras: Jack Quinn struck first for the Sabres on the power play early in the first, and Tage Thompson made it 2-0 late in the second. Corey Perry got the Kings on the board on the power play less than two minutes later. Andre Lee tied it up early in the third, but that was the last goal the Kings would get. Thompson struck again on the power play with less than seven minutes left to put the Sabres ahead for good.

The Kings had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Kings win about seven in ten. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was the difference, stopping 27 of 29. The Kings hit two posts and still lost. Anton Forsberg stopped 28 of 31 for the Kings. The Sabres moved to 7-4-3, seventh in the Atlantic, while the Kings dropped to 4-7-2, seventh in the Pacific.

items.text: Tage Thompson passed René Robert for ninth on the Sabres’ all-time goals list, with 223.
Three straight wins for the Sabres.
Artemi Panarin had a point in all nine of his games against Buffalo since 2023-24, and that run ended.
The Sabres have beaten the Kings four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
